name: sctp_process_asconf_param
prose: Static function returning an __be16 SCTP error cause (SCTP_ERROR_NO_ERROR on success) for one ADD_IP, DEL_IP or SET_PRIMARY parameter of a received ASCONF chunk. Checks in order: SCTP_ERROR_UNKNOWN_PARAM if the parameter type is none of those three; SCTP_ERROR_PROTO_VIOLATION if the embedded address parameter's length exceeds the parameter length minus the sctp_addip_param header; SCTP_ERROR_DNS_FAILED if the embedded type is not an IPv6/IPv4 address parameter, if the association's peer does not support that family, if sctp_get_af_specific returns NULL, if from_addr_param fails, or if the address is not the wildcard and addr_valid fails. Then by type. ADD_IP: a wildcard address is replaced by asconf->source; SCTP_ERROR_REQ_REFUSED if security_sctp_bind_connect returns nonzero; SCTP_ERROR_RSRC_LOW if sctp_assoc_add_peer returns NULL; otherwise the new SCTP_UNCONFIRMED peer gets its heartbeat timer reset, asoc->new_transport is set to it and NO_ERROR is returned. DEL_IP: SCTP_ERROR_DEL_LAST_IP if asoc->peer.transport_count is 1; SCTP_ERROR_DEL_SRC_IP if the address exactly equals asconf->source; for a wildcard address it makes asconf->transport the primary, deletes all other peers with sctp_assoc_del_nonprimary_peers and returns NO_ERROR; otherwise SCTP_ERROR_DNS_FAILED if no peer has that address, SCTP_ERROR_REQ_REFUSED if the matching peer is asconf->transport, else the peer is removed with sctp_assoc_rm_peer and NO_ERROR is returned. SET_PRIMARY: a wildcard address is replaced by sctp_source(asconf); SCTP_ERROR_REQ_REFUSED if security_sctp_bind_connect returns nonzero; SCTP_ERROR_DNS_FAILED if no peer matches; otherwise that peer becomes the primary and NO_ERROR is returned.
note: slice cut the head (function starts at sm_make_chunk.c:3048). Prior prose claimed the association is left unchanged on every error path; dropped because DEL_IP wildcard mutates before returning NO_ERROR and sctp_assoc_add_peer failure effects are not visible here. Checked against 3048-3197.

name: sctp_cmd_interpreter
prose: Static function that executes the queued side-effect commands for one SCTP state-machine event. chunk is set to event_arg unless event_type is SCTP_EVENT_T_TIMEOUT (1304-1305). error is a local initialised to 0 (1301), not a parameter. It loops over sctp_next_cmd(commands) until NULL and dispatches on cmd->verb; an unrecognised verb only logs a warning. Commands include association creation/deletion, state change, timer start/restart/stop (taking or dropping an association reference when the timer was or was not pending), queuing replies on asoc->outqueue (SCTP_CMD_REPLY and SCTP_CMD_SEND_MSG cork the queue if it was not corked and remember that in local_cork), packet send, transport and heartbeat updates, ULP event delivery. These verbs set error: SCTP_CMD_REPORT_TSN, GEN_SACK, PROCESS_SACK, PEER_INIT and ASSOC_SHKEY take the callee's return value; GEN_INIT_ACK, GEN_COOKIE_ECHO and GEN_SHUTDOWN set -ENOMEM when the chunk cannot be built; REPORT_ERROR copies cmd->obj.error. After each command, if error is nonzero, the remaining commands are drained without being executed, the chunk of each remaining SCTP_CMD_REPLY is freed with sctp_chunk_free, and the loop ends. After the loop: if asoc is non-NULL, event_type is SCTP_EVENT_T_CHUNK and chunk is non-NULL, the outqueue is uncorked only when chunk->end_of_packet or chunk->singleton; otherwise, if local_cork is set, the outqueue is uncorked. sp->data_ready_signalled is cleared if it was set. There is one return, at the end, returning error (0 or the value last stored by one of the verbs above, not necessarily a negative errno).
note: slice cut the head and tail; the real function is sm_sideeffect.c:1282-1832 (single return at 1831). Same prose as the tail-slice record for the same function. Checked 1282-1832 line by line.

note: slice cut the head; real function sm_sideeffect.c:1282-1832. Reviewer was right: there is no error parameter, error is a local initialised to 0 at line 1301 so the old 'nonzero error on entry returned unchanged' claim was false; prose rewritten.

name: sctp_getsockopt_peer_addrs
prose: Static getsockopt helper that copies the peer transport addresses of one association to user memory. Precondition: len is the caller's buffer length, optval points to a user buffer that begins with a struct sctp_getaddrs, optlen is a user pointer. Returns -EINVAL if len is less than sizeof(struct sctp_getaddrs); -EFAULT if copy_from_user of that header fails; -EINVAL if sctp_id2assoc(sk, getaddrs.assoc_id) returns NULL (no matching association). Then, for each transport in asoc->peer.transport_addr_list, the address is converted for the socket family with the family's addr_to_user callback and copied to optval starting at offsetof(struct sctp_getaddrs, addrs): the function returns -ENOMEM if the space left is smaller than that address, or -EFAULT if copy_to_user fails (addresses already copied before the failure stay in the user buffer). After the list is walked it stores the count of addresses copied in the addr_num field of optval (-EFAULT if put_user fails), stores the number of bytes used (offset of the addrs field plus the copied addresses) in *optlen (-EFAULT if put_user fails) and returns 0; an association with no transports yields count 0 and return 0.
note: Checked 6168-6217. Reviewers' round-2 claim that optlen is never used and that a put_user to assoc_id is omitted is wrong: put_user(cnt, addr_num) is at 6210 and put_user(bytes_copied, optlen) at 6213; the round-1 claim about -EINVAL was about an older prose and the current prose already states it.

name: sctp_wait_for_connect
prose: Static function that waits for an association to become established. Precondition: the caller holds the socket lock of asoc->base.sk and *timeo_p is the timeout in jiffies. It takes an association reference with sctp_association_hold and releases it with sctp_association_put on every exit from the loop (all exits reach the out label or break out of the loop to it), and calls finish_wait there. Each loop iteration, in this order: if *timeo_p is 0 it returns -EINPROGRESS (this test is made before the state tests, so it applies even when the association is already ESTABLISHED, and it is reached when a previous sleep left *timeo_p at 0); if sk->sk_shutdown has RCV_SHUTDOWN it returns 0; if sk->sk_err is set, asoc->state is at least SCTP_STATE_SHUTDOWN_PENDING or asoc->base.dead is set it returns -ETIMEDOUT when asoc->init_err_counter + 1 > asoc->max_init_attempts and -ECONNREFUSED otherwise; if a signal is pending it returns sock_intr_errno(*timeo_p) (-ERESTARTSYS or -EINTR); if the state is ESTABLISHED it returns 0; otherwise it releases the socket lock, sleeps with schedule_timeout(current_timeo), retakes the lock, and if sk is no longer asoc->base.sk it returns the same -ETIMEDOUT/-ECONNREFUSED value without updating *timeo_p; otherwise it stores the remaining time in *timeo_p and loops.
note: Checked 9340-9402. Reviewer round 15 was right: the sk != asoc->base.sk exit (9374-9375) jumps to do_error before *timeo_p is updated at 9377; prior prose said it was updated after each sleep. Reviewer round 2 (EINPROGRESS after timeout) and original (0 on RCV_SHUTDOWN) are covered by the rewritten prose.

name: sctp_process_strreset_resp
prose: Processes one stream-reset response parameter (param.v as struct sctp_strreset_resp). Every return statement in the function returns NULL; the outcome is delivered through *evp and association state. It returns NULL without touching *evp or the reconf state when: sctp_chunk_lookup_strreset_param finds no outstanding request for resp->response_seq, or SCTP_STRRESET_TEST says that request's type is not pending; the result is SCTP_STRRESET_IN_PROGRESS; the request is a TSN reset and the parameter length is not sizeof(struct sctp_strreset_resptsn); or the request is an IN request or ADD_IN_STREAMS request and the result is SCTP_STRRESET_PERFORMED. Otherwise: flags is 0 for PERFORMED, SCTP_STREAM_RESET_DENIED for DENIED and SCTP_STREAM_RESET_FAILED for any other result, and by request type: OUT request (resets mid/mid_uo of the listed or all out streams only if PERFORMED, sets all out streams to SCTP_STREAM_OPEN, *evp = stream-reset event with SCTP_STREAM_RESET_OUTGOING_SSN); IN request (*evp = stream-reset event with INCOMING_SSN); TSN request (if PERFORMED reports FTSN, reinitialises the peer tsn map from the sender's next TSN, frees the outqueue's sacked/abandoned chunks, sets next_tsn, ctsn_ack_point and adv_peer_ack_point from the receiver's next TSN and zeroes the stream mids; sets all out streams to open; *evp = assoc-reset event); ADD_OUT_STREAMS (if PERFORMED opens the added streams, otherwise migrates the added streams' queued data and sets stream->outcnt back to outcnt - number_of_streams; *evp = stream-change event); ADD_IN_STREAMS (*evp = stream-change event). Each *evp value comes from a ulpevent constructor called with GFP_ATOMIC and may be NULL on allocation failure. After the type-specific work it clears the request type with SCTP_STRRESET_CLEAR, increments asoc->strreset_outseq and, if asoc->strreset_outstanding is zero, deletes the reconf timer of asoc->strreset_chunk->transport (calling sctp_transport_put if the timer was pending), drops the reference on asoc->strreset_chunk with sctp_chunk_put and sets it to NULL.
note: slice cut the head (function starts at stream.c:935). Checked 935-1113. Old prose omitted the DENIED/FAILED handling and the non-PERFORMED ADD_OUT rollback; 'always returns NULL' is true (all six returns are NULL) and is kept in the 'every return statement' form.

name: sctp_process_strreset_addstrm_in
prose: Processes an incoming ADD_IN_STREAMS reset request (param.v as struct sctp_strreset_addstrm); evp is not used or written. request_seq is addstrm->request_seq. If request_seq is more than 0 ahead of asoc->strreset_inseq or more than 2 behind it (TSN_lt comparisons), result is SCTP_STRRESET_ERR_BAD_SEQNO and it returns sctp_make_strreset_resp(asoc, result, request_seq) without changing state. If request_seq is older than strreset_inseq but inside that window, it reads the stored asoc->strreset_result[strreset_inseq - request_seq - 1]: it returns NULL if that stored result is SCTP_STRRESET_PERFORMED, otherwise a response chunk carrying the stored result, again without changing state. Otherwise it increments asoc->strreset_inseq and then: if SCTP_ENABLE_CHANGE_ASSOC_REQ is clear in asoc->strreset_enable the result stays SCTP_STRRESET_DENIED; if asoc->strreset_outstanding is set the result is SCTP_STRRESET_ERR_IN_PROGRESS; if the requested stream count is 0, or stream->outcnt plus it exceeds SCTP_MAX_STREAM, or sctp_stream_alloc_out fails, or sctp_make_strreset_addstrm fails, the result is SCTP_STRRESET_DENIED; in each of these cases the result is recorded with sctp_update_strreset_result, stream->outcnt is not changed, and the return value is sctp_make_strreset_resp(asoc, result, request_seq) (NULL if that allocation fails). On success it stores the new ADD_OUT_STREAMS request chunk in asoc->strreset_chunk and takes an extra reference on it with sctp_chunk_hold, sets the ADD_OUT_STREAMS flag, sets stream->outcnt to the old value plus the count, records SCTP_STRRESET_PERFORMED and returns that request chunk (not a response chunk); the caller owns one reference to the returned chunk.
note: Checked 870-933. Reviewers' round-1 claim (NULL on old PERFORMED) is already covered; round-2 claim about an in-flight completion block is wrong, no such block exists in this function (870-933). Prose slightly corrected: the success return is the request chunk, and the failing branches differ in which result they record.

name: sctp_intl_reasm
prose: Static function that handles a data ulpevent in the interleaved (I-DATA) reassembly path. Precondition: event is a data event owned by the caller and not on any list; ulpq->asoc is valid. If (event->msg_flags & SCTP_DATA_FRAG_MASK) is SCTP_DATA_NOT_FRAG it sets MSG_EOR on event and returns event itself (ownership stays with the caller). Otherwise it stores event in ulpq->reasm with sctp_intl_store_reasm (the list now owns it), then, if the per-stream sin->pd_mode is set and event->mid == sin->mid and event->fsn == sin->fsn, it tries sctp_intl_retrieve_partial; if that returns NULL (or was not tried) it tries sctp_intl_retrieve_reassembled. It returns whichever of those returned: a reassembled event built by sctp_make_reassembled_event (which carries MSG_EOR when the last fragment was assembled, and does not carry it when only a prefix of the message was built, either because pd_point was reached in sctp_intl_retrieve_reassembled or because sctp_intl_retrieve_partial ended before the last fragment), or NULL when neither found anything or sctp_make_reassembled_event failed to allocate.
note: Checked 348-370 and the callees at 180-346. Old prose wording 'MSG_EOR set only when complete message' is kept in substance; added that retrieve_partial also sets MSG_EOR when it reaches the last fragment. Reviewer claims about the NOT_FRAG case and partial delivery are already covered by the text.

name: sctp_enqueue_event
prose: Static function that delivers a list of ulpevents to the socket. Precondition: skb_list is non-empty; only its first skb is inspected. sk is ulpq->asoc->base.sk. It frees (sctp_queue_purge_ulpevents on the whole skb_list) and returns 0 when either sk->sk_shutdown has RCV_SHUTDOWN and (also SEND_SHUTDOWN or the first event is not a notification), or the first event is not enabled by ulpq->asoc->subscribe (sctp_ulpevent_is_enabled). So with RCV_SHUTDOWN and SEND_SHUTDOWN both set even notifications are purged, and with only RCV_SHUTDOWN set notifications pass this test and only non-notification events are purged. Otherwise, for a non-notification first event it records the napi id and incoming cpu on the socket (sk_mark_napi_id, sk_incoming_cpu_update), splices the whole list to the tail of sk->sk_receive_queue (skb_list becomes empty), and if sp->data_ready_signalled was clear sets it and calls sk->sk_data_ready(sk) once; it returns 1.
note: Checked 469-507. Both reviewer claims were wrong: the old prose already said that with RCV_SHUTDOWN and SEND_SHUTDOWN notifications are purged (480-483, 503-506). Prose kept, details on the napi/cpu marking added.

name: sctp_sched_get_sched_value_placeholder
note: No function of this name or any 'sched_value' symbol exists in net/sctp/stream_sched.c (grep for 'placeholder' and 'sched_value' returns nothing); the old prose was only 'unused'. Not a function in the source.

name: smc_llc_process_srv_delete_link
prose: Static void function that handles a delete-link message queued on the local LLC flow, for a link group lgr. It takes lgr->llc_conf_mutex for writing (down_write) first, then takes the queued entry with smc_llc_flow_qentry_clr(&lgr->llc_flow_lcl) (so the entry is cleared while the mutex is held). There is a single exit (label out) which does up_write on the mutex and kfree(qentry); there are no early returns. If the message has SMC_LLC_FLAG_DEL_LINK_ALL it calls smc_llc_send_link_delete_all(lgr, true, reason from the message) and smc_lgr_terminate_sched(lgr) and goes to out. Otherwise it searches lgr->lnk[0..SMC_LINKS_PER_LGR_MAX-1] for a link whose link_id equals del_llc->link_num; if none matches it goes to out with no other effect. If a link matches: if smc_link_downing(&lnk_del->state) is true it calls smc_switch_conns(lgr, lnk_del, false) and, only if that returns nonzero, smc_wr_tx_wait_no_pending_sends(lnk_del); then, if lgr->list is not empty, it sends the message back on the receiving link qentry->link with smc_llc_send_message and, only if that send returns 0, waits with smc_llc_wait for an SMC_LLC_DELETE_LINK message and, if one arrives (non-NULL), discards the flow's entry with smc_llc_flow_qentry_del. It then calls smcr_link_clear(lnk_del, true). It counts active links: if exactly one it sets the lgr type SMC_LGR_SINGLE; if zero it sets SMC_LGR_NONE and calls smc_lgr_terminate_sched; with two or more the type is not changed by this function. Finally, if lgr->type is SMC_LGR_SINGLE (checked after the update, so also when it was already SINGLE) and lgr->list is not empty, it calls smc_llc_add_link_local on the receiving link.
note: slice cut the head (function at smc_llc.c:1698-1764). Checked line by line. Old prose was mostly right; corrected that smc_wr_tx_wait_no_pending_sends depends on smc_switch_conns returning nonzero, that the wait result is only discarded when non-NULL, and the DEL_LINK_ALL arguments. Reviewer round-2 claim (mutex released before qentry taken) was wrong: down_write at 1706 precedes qentry_clr at 1707; reviewer round-1 claims (conditional echo/wait, no-match path) were right.

name: rpcauth_prune_expired
prose: Static function that scans the global cred_unused LRU list and moves reclaimable credentials onto the list free. Precondition: the caller holds rpc_credcache_lock (rpcauth_cache_do_shrink takes it around the call), free is an initialised list head, nr_to_scan is non-negative (a negative value would make the count never reach zero, so the whole list is scanned). The function does not release that lock; rpcauth_unhash_cred briefly takes the credential cache's own lock. It examines entries from the head of cred_unused; it stops when the list ends or when the remaining scan count reaches zero before an entry is examined, so at most nr_to_scan entries are examined (none when nr_to_scan is 0). For each examined entry: if refcount_read(&cred->cr_count) > 1 it is removed from the LRU list (rpcauth_lru_remove_locked) and kept; else if cr_expire lies within the 60 second window ending at jiffies (time_in_range) it is left in place; else if rpcauth_unhash_cred returns false (cred not hashed, or unhash refused) it is left in place; otherwise it is removed from the LRU list, counted and appended to free. The return value is the number of credentials appended to free, or SHRINK_STOP when that number is zero. The credentials on free are left for the caller to dispose of (rpcauth_cache_do_shrink calls rpcauth_destroy_credlist).
note: Checked auth.c:421-455 and rpcauth_unhash_cred at 270-282. Reviewer round-2 claim (nr_to_scan+1 entries) was wrong: nr_to_scan-- == 0 breaks before the entry is examined (435-436). Old claim about the reference held by the hash table was removed as not verifiable in this function.

name: call_transmit
prose: Static RPC state function for the transmit step. If rpc_task_transmitted(task) is true it calls rpc_task_handle_transmitted(task), which calls xprt_end_transmit(task) and sets task->tk_action to call_transmit_status, and returns without touching tk_status. Otherwise it sets task->tk_action to call_transmit_status, then: if xprt_prepare_transmit(task) returns false it returns with tk_status unchanged and without calling xprt_end_transmit; otherwise it sets tk_status to 0 and, if RPC_TASK_NEED_XMIT is set in tk_runstate, then if the transport is not connected (xprt_connected false) it sets tk_status to -ENOTCONN and returns without calling xprt_transmit or xprt_end_transmit, and if it is connected calls xprt_transmit(task). In every remaining case (connected with NEED_XMIT set, or NEED_XMIT clear) it then calls xprt_end_transmit(task); xprt_transmit is called only when NEED_XMIT is set.
note: Checked clnt.c:2292-2311 and rpc_task_handle_transmitted at 2046-2050. Reviewers were right: old prose said tk_action unchanged on the already-transmitted path (it is set to call_transmit_status) and mis-described the NEED_XMIT-clear path.

name: call_transmit_status
prose: Static RPC state function run after a transmit attempt. It first sets task->tk_action to call_status. If rpc_task_transmitted(task) is true it sets tk_status to 0, calls xprt_request_wait_receive(task) and returns without calling rpc_check_timeout. Otherwise it switches on task->tk_status: -EBADMSG sets tk_status 0 and tk_action call_encode; -ENOMEM and -ENOBUFS call rpc_delay(task, HZ>>2) and then, like -EBADSLT and -EAGAIN, set tk_action to call_transmit and tk_status to 0; -EHOSTDOWN, -ENETDOWN, -EHOSTUNREACH, -ENETUNREACH, -EPERM and any status not listed leave tk_action as call_status and tk_status unchanged; -ECONNREFUSED with RPC_IS_SOFTCONN(task) true calls trace_xprt_ping first when the message's p_proc is 0 (NULL), then rpc_call_rpcerror(task, tk_status) and returns without calling rpc_check_timeout; -ECONNREFUSED otherwise, and -ECONNRESET, -ECONNABORTED, -EADDRINUSE, -ENOTCONN and -EPIPE set tk_action to call_bind and tk_status to 0. On every path except the transmitted early return and the soft-connection -ECONNREFUSED return, rpc_check_timeout(task) is then called.
note: Checked clnt.c:2317-2378. Prose kept in substance; reviewers' claims (call_bind for connection errors, check_timeout skipped on transmitted path) are already in the text. Fixed 'p_proc is NULL' wording to the actual test (!p_proc).

name: xprt_sock_sendmsg
prose: Writes an xdr_buf to a socket in up to three pieces (head, page data, tail), with an optional stream record marker. Parameters: sock, msg, xdr, base (starting offset in the buffer), marker (record marker, 0 for none), sent_p (out). It sets *sent_p to 0 first. Returns -ENOTSOCK if sock is NULL. Otherwise it sets MSG_MORE in msg->msg_flags and sends, in order, the remaining part of xdr->head[0] (together with the marker via xprt_send_rm_and_kvec when marker is nonzero), the remaining part of the page data (xprt_send_pagedata) and the remaining part of xdr->tail[0], skipping a piece when base is already past it; MSG_MORE is cleared before the piece that contains the last remaining byte. After a piece it continues to the next only if the send returned exactly the piece's length (compared as unsigned) and more data remains. If the tail is already entirely before base it returns 0 with *sent_p holding the bytes sent by earlier pieces. On any other exit a positive send result is added to *sent_p and the function returns 0, so a short send (fewer bytes than requested) also returns 0 with *sent_p holding the total sent; a negative result from the send call is returned as is (bytes sent by earlier pieces remain in *sent_p).
note: The packet slice (socklib.c:253-278) is the tail of xprt_sock_sendmsg (defined at socklib.c:218-278); the old record named it 'unnamed-send-helper'. Fixed under the real name. Checked the whole function.

name: xprt_request_transmit
prose: Static function that sends one request req on its transport and dequeues it from the transmit queue in most outcomes. snd_task is not used in the body; all waking and flag changes use task = req->rq_task. is_retrans = RPC_WAS_SENT(task) is sampled at entry before RPC_TASK_SENT is set. Returns -ENOTCONN, with no other change, if XPRT_CLOSE_WAIT is set in xprt->state. When req->rq_bytes_sent is 0 it first checks: if xprt_request_data_received(task) status is 0, else if rpcauth_xmit_need_reencode(task) status is -EBADMSG, else if RPC_SIGNALLED(task) status is -ERESTARTSYS; in those three cases rq_ntrans is not changed, and control goes to the dequeue step. Otherwise it increments req->rq_ntrans, samples xprt->connect_cookie and calls xprt->ops->send_request(req); if that returns nonzero it decrements rq_ntrans, traces and returns that value without dequeuing or waking. On success it increments task->tk_client->cl_stats->rpcretrans if is_retrans was true, calls xprt_inject_disconnect, sets RPC_TASK_SENT in task->tk_flags, updates xprt->stat counters under xprt->transport_lock, sets req->rq_connect_cookie to the sampled cookie, and goes to the dequeue step with status 0. The dequeue step traces, calls xprt_request_dequeue_transmit(task), wakes task on xprt->sending with that status (rpc_wake_up_queued_task_set_status) and returns the status (0, -EBADMSG or -ERESTARTSYS). The function does not unpin req.
note: Checked xprt.c:1542-1608. Reviewer round-15 claim: partly right about the name (is_retrans is a local copy of RPC_WAS_SENT(task) taken at entry, so behaviour is the same), but wrong that wakeups target snd_task: line 1606 wakes 'task' = req->rq_task; snd_task is unused. Round-2 claim (EBADMSG/ERESTARTSYS are dequeued) right and already in the prose; round-1 claim about rq_ntrans rollback on ENOTCONN is moot since it is not incremented before those returns.

name: rpcrdma_reply_handler
prose: Handles one received RPC-over-RDMA reply rep. It first sets xprt->reestablish_timeout to 0 if nonzero. It decodes the fixed header (xid, version, credits, proc) with xdr_inline_decode; if the 4-word header cannot be decoded it takes the short-reply exit. The credit value from the wire is sanitised: 0 becomes 1 and values above r_xprt->rx_ep->re_max_requests are clamped to that. If rep->rr_vers != rpcrdma_version it takes the bad-version exit. If rpcrdma_is_bcall(r_xprt, rep) is true it returns immediately, without releasing rep and without posting receives. Otherwise it takes xprt->queue_lock and looks up the request by xid with xprt_lookup_rqst; if none exists it unlocks, traces, releases rep with rpcrdma_rep_put and posts receives (no-request exit). If one exists it pins it (xprt_pin_rqst), unlocks, calls rpcrdma_update_cwnd when buf->rb_credits != credits, puts any previous req->rl_reply with rpcrdma_rep_put, stores rep in req->rl_reply and rep->rr_rqst, calls frwr_reminv if the work completion has IB_WC_WITH_INVALIDATE, and then, if req->rl_registered is not empty (whether or not an invalidate flag was set), calls frwr_unmap_async (the LocalInv completion completes the RPC), otherwise calls rpcrdma_complete_rqst(rep). The short-reply and bad-version exits release rep with rpcrdma_rep_put and set credits to buf->rb_credits. All exits other than the backchannel one then call rpcrdma_post_recvs(r_xprt, credits + (buf->rb_bc_srv_max_requests << 1)) and return.
note: slice cut the head (function at rpc_rdma.c:1500-1592). Reviewer round-15 right: frwr_unmap_async is called whenever rl_registered is non-empty after the optional frwr_reminv (1562-1565), not only on an invalidate completion; prose rewritten. Old precondition about the caller holding exactly one reference was dropped as not verifiable here.

name: pcl_process_nonpayloads
prose: Calls actor on each region of an xdr_buf that lies outside the payload chunks of a chunk list. Parameters: pcl (struct svc_rdma_pcl), xdr (struct xdr_buf, not an xdr_stream), actor (int (*)(const struct xdr_buf *, void *)), data. If pcl has no first chunk or the first chunk's ch_payload_length is 0, it returns actor(xdr, data) directly, whatever that value is (it may be positive). Otherwise it processes the region from offset 0 of length first-chunk ch_position, then the region between the end of each chunk and the ch_position of the next chunk, walking while the next chunk exists and has a nonzero ch_payload_length, and finally the region from the end of the last visited chunk to xdr->len. Each region goes through pcl_process_region, which does nothing and returns 0 for a zero-length region, returns -EMSGSIZE if xdr_buf_subsegment fails, and otherwise returns actor on the sub-buffer. The function returns the first negative value from pcl_process_region (stopping there, later regions are not processed) and returns 0 if no region returned a negative value; positive values returned by actor for a region inside the chain are not checked and do not stop the walk.
note: Real function name is pcl_process_nonpayloads (svc_rdma_pcl.c:265-306); the packet used an invented unnamed name and the slice cut the head. Checked 232-306. Old prose said xdr is an xdr_stream (it is struct xdr_buf), and omitted -EMSGSIZE and the unchecked positive actor returns; the lock/reference claim was dropped as unverified.

name: tipc_crypto_clone_msg
prose: Static inline void function that sends a clone of a message. It calls skb_clone(_skb, GFP_ATOMIC); if that returns NULL nothing else happens. Otherwise it sets TIPC_SKB_CB(clone)->xmit_type to type and calls tipc_crypto_xmit(net, &clone, b, dst, __dnode), ignoring its return value. If the clone pointer is still non-NULL afterwards (tipc_crypto_xmit returned 0, which includes the no-encryption case) it passes the clone to b->media->send_msg(net, clone, b, dst). If tipc_crypto_xmit returned -EINPROGRESS or -EBUSY it sets the clone pointer to NULL and this function neither sends nor frees the clone (the encryption callback is expected to continue); on other errors tipc_crypto_xmit frees the clone and sets the pointer to NULL. The function itself does not modify or free _skb.
note: Checked crypto.c:1649-1663 and tipc_crypto_xmit exit paths at 1766-1788. Reviewers were right about failure/async paths; prose already covered them. Removed the unprovable 'always untouched' for _skb (clones share data buffers) and replaced it with what this function itself does.

name: tipc_crypto_rcv
prose: Decrypts a received encrypted TIPC message *skb for crypto context rx (may be NULL) on bearer b and returns a status; it frees *skb on failure. It reads tx_key from the encryption header at the start of (*skb)->data. Key selection: if rx is NULL or tx_key is KEY_MASTER it goes to pick_tx; else if tx_key equals rx->key.active, pending or passive it decrypts with that rx slot; else if tipc_crypto_key_try_align(rx, tx_key) succeeds it decrypts; otherwise pick_tx. At pick_tx it calls tipc_crypto_key_pick_tx(tx, rx, *skb, tx_key); if that returns an aead it decrypts with it, else it goes to exit with rc = -ENOKEY. At decrypt it takes rcu_read_lock, takes an aead reference with tipc_aead_get(rx->aead[tx_key]) if none was picked, calls tipc_aead_decrypt(net, aead, *skb, b) and drops the RCU lock. At exit the stats are those of rx if non-NULL, else of the tx context. rc 0: STAT_OK, then tipc_crypto_rcv_complete(net, aead, b, skb, rc). -EINPROGRESS or -EBUSY: STAT_ASYNC, *skb is set to NULL and rc is returned without calling rcv_complete (the asynchronous completion continues). -ENOKEY: STAT_NOK and STAT_NOKEYS, *skb is freed and set to NULL, and if rx is non-NULL rx->nokey is set to whether rx->skey and the next key slot are both empty and one rx->node reference is dropped (tipc_node_put); rc is returned without calling rcv_complete and without releasing an aead reference in this function. Any other rc (including -EBADMSG, which also bumps STAT_BADMSGS): STAT_NOK then tipc_crypto_rcv_complete(net, aead, b, skb, rc); rc is returned.
note: The packet name tipc_crypto_decrypt does not exist; 'decrypt:' is a label inside the real function tipc_crypto_rcv (crypto.c:1813-1894) and the slice cut its head. Fixed under the real name. Reviewer round-15 claim (ENOKEY path returns without releasing the aead reference) is right: old prose said the reference was held 'for the duration of the call'; new prose avoids that and only states what this function does. Rcv_complete behaviour (aead put, node put) is in lines 1996-2003, not repeated here.

name: tipc_link_bc_init_rcv
prose: Void function that may initialise the receive state of a broadcast receive link l from the header hdr of a message received from the peer. It reads mtyp = msg_type(hdr) and peers_snd_nxt = msg_bc_snd_nxt(hdr). If tipc_link_is_up(l) it returns without modifying l. Otherwise, if msg_user(hdr) is BCAST_PROTOCOL it sets l->rcv_nxt to peers_snd_nxt and l->state to LINK_ESTABLISHED and returns. Otherwise it returns without modifying l if l->peer_caps has TIPC_BCAST_SYNCH or msg_peer_node_is_up(hdr) is true. In the remaining case (link not up, message not BCAST_PROTOCOL, peer lacks TIPC_BCAST_SYNCH, peer node not up) it sets l->rcv_nxt to peers_snd_nxt only if mtyp is RESET_MSG or ACTIVATE_MSG, and leaves l->state unchanged.
note: slice cut the head (function at link.c:2377-2400). Reviewer claim (legacy RESET/ACTIVATE only when peer lacks BCAST_SYNCH and peer node is down) matches the code and the old prose; but the old prose also said the function only reads through its pointers, which is false (it writes l->rcv_nxt and l->state), so the prose was rewritten for clarity.

name: __tipc_nl_compat_dumpit
prose: Static function that runs a netlink dump callback synchronously for the legacy compat API and formats its output into msg->rep. Returns -ENOMEM if nlmsg_new fails (nothing else done) or if __tipc_dump_start fails (the new skb is freed first). Allocates the attribute array attrbuf with kcalloc (-ENOMEM, via the common exit, if that fails). If the request netlink header has a payload (nlmsg_len > 0) it parses it with nlmsg_parse_deprecated and exits with that error if parsing fails. It then repeats: call cmd->dumpit(buf, &cb); a negative result is the error; otherwise parse every nlmsg in buf and call cmd->format(msg, attrbuf), exiting with the first parse or format error, and with -EMSGSIZE if tipc_skb_tailroom(msg->rep) is at most 1; after each pass the dump buffer is reset; the loop ends when dumpit returns 0, then err is 0. The common exit frees attrbuf, calls tipc_dump_done(&cb) and frees buf. If err is -EMSGSIZE it returns 0 instead: and, if TIPC_SKB_MAX - msg->rep->len is at most 1 and the byte at the reply's tail pointer is non-NUL, it first writes the REPLY_TRUNCATED string with sprintf just before the tail. Any other err is returned unchanged.
note: The packet slice (netlink_compat.c:252-505) held only the tail of this function; the real function is __tipc_nl_compat_dumpit at netlink_compat.c:178-277 and exists, so it is fixed rather than dropped. Checked the whole function.

name: tipc_node_add_conn
prose: Records a socket connection (port, peer_port) on the node entry for dnode. If in_own_node(net, dnode) it returns 0 and records nothing. Otherwise it looks the node up with tipc_node_find; if none exists it logs a warning and returns -EHOSTUNREACH. It then allocates a tipc_sock_conn with kmalloc(GFP_ATOMIC); if that fails it returns -EHOSTUNREACH (after dropping the node reference). On success it fills in peer_node, port and peer_port, appends the entry to node->conn_sks under tipc_node_write_lock/unlock (with no check for an existing entry), drops the node reference with tipc_node_put and returns 0. No lock is held on return and the node reference taken by tipc_node_find is released on both paths after it.
note: Checked node.c:692-721. The old prose is correct in substance; made the in_own_node check and the no-duplicate-check explicit. Contract left empty: pointer and list state involved.

name: __tipc_sendstream
prose: Sends stream or seqpacket data of length dlen from msg m on a TIPC socket; the caller holds the socket lock. If dlen > INT_MAX it returns -EMSGSIZE. If m->msg_name is non-NULL and sk->sk_state is TIPC_OPEN, it returns exactly what __tipc_sendmsg(sock, m, dlen) returns (a byte count or a negative errno), and, when dlen is nonzero and equals that return value, first updates tsk->peer_caps and tsk->snt_unacked. Otherwise it loops (at least once, also when dlen is 0) while sent < dlen and rc is 0: wait with tipc_wait_for_cond until the link is not congested, the connection is not congested and the socket is connected (a nonzero result breaks); send = min(dlen - sent, TIPC_MAX_USER_MSG_SIZE); if the Nagle conditions hold (tsk->oneway++ >= nagle_start, maxnagle nonzero, send <= maxnagle) it calls tipc_msg_append (a negative result breaks; if the accumulated blocks are at most 64 and an ack is expected it records the backlog, adds send to sent and breaks without transmitting), otherwise it calls tipc_msg_build (a result different from send breaks); then tipc_node_xmit, where -ELINKCONG is turned into 0 and sets tsk->cong_link_cnt to 1, and on rc 0 it updates snt_unacked and snd_backlog and adds send to sent. It returns sent if sent is nonzero, otherwise rc. rc may therefore be 0, a negative errno from the wait, tipc_msg_append, tipc_msg_build or tipc_node_xmit, or a positive value (the tipc_msg_append block count on the Nagle break, or a short tipc_msg_build count) when sent is still 0; a partial positive sent is returned even if a later step failed.
note: Checked socket.c:1556-1638. Reviewer round-15 right: with dlen 0 on the Nagle path rc from tipc_msg_append (positive) can be returned because sent stays 0 (1596-1604, 1638); old prose claimed only 0 or negative. Round-2 claim (dlen > INT_MAX) is covered: old prose did handle -EMSGSIZE; the precondition 'dlen may be any size_t' was already in. Old claims about locks being released/reacquired and no references to release were dropped as not verifiable here.

name: tls_sw_sendmsg_locked
prose: Sends the data in msg over a software kernel-TLS transmit context; the caller holds the socket lock, and the size parameter is not used (the loop runs while msg_data_left(msg) is nonzero). It returns -EINVAL immediately if MSG_EOR is set together with MSG_MORE. If msg->msg_controllen is nonzero it calls tls_process_cmsg: -EINPROGRESS counts as one pending async operation, -EAGAIN is ignored, and any other nonzero result jumps to the end (async wait skipped). Per loop iteration: a pending sk_err gives ret = -sk_err and exit; a missing open record from tls_get_rec gives -ENOMEM and exit; if the socket send buffer is not free it sets SOCK_NOSPACE and waits; if the plaintext record is already full the data is not copied and the record goes to the verdict step; tls_alloc_encrypted_msg failing with an error other than -ENOSPC waits for memory (-ENOSPC only shrinks the amount to copy). With MSG_SPLICE_PAGES the data is taken by tls_sw_sendmsg_splice (a negative result exits). Otherwise, for non-kvec data, a full record or eor, and a non-async-capable context, it first tries zero-copy; if sk_msg_zerocopy_from_iter fails it falls back to a regular copy; after zero-copy it runs bpf_exec_tx_verdict: -EINPROGRESS counts as async, -ENOMEM waits for memory and retries, -ENOSPC with an open record returns the bytes copied so far if the record is corked (ret set to 0) and otherwise rolls back the iterator and uses the regular copy path, -EAGAIN continues, other errors exit. The regular path calls tls_clone_plaintext_msg (any error other than -ENOSPC exits; -ENOSPC shrinks the copy) and sk_msg_memcopy_from_iter (a negative result trims the records and exits). When a record is full or eor is set, bpf_exec_tx_verdict runs: -EINPROGRESS counts as async, -ENOMEM goes to sk_stream_wait_memory and the loop retries rather than returning -ENOMEM, -EAGAIN continues, -ENOSPC becomes 0 and exits, other errors exit. A failing sk_stream_wait_memory exits with its error after trimming both records. At exit, if async encryptions are pending and either zero-copy was used or eor is set, tls_encrypt_async_wait is called and its error replaces ret and clears the copied count; scheduled transmits are then pushed with tls_tx_records. The final ret is passed through sk_stream_error and the function returns the copied byte count if it is positive, otherwise ret (0, a negative errno, or a left-over -EAGAIN/-EINPROGRESS status).
note: Checked tls_sw.c:1050-1304. Reviewer round-15 right: a tx verdict of -ENOMEM jumps to wait_for_memory and retries (1248-1249, 1177-1178), it is not returned directly; reviewer round-2 (corked -ENOSPC returns copied bytes, not 0) is consistent with 'return copied > 0 ? copied : ret' at 1303: old prose already said the byte count is returned, so this one is mostly a misreading, but the wording is now explicit. Old claims about pages remaining owned by TLS and socket memory charging were removed as not checkable in this function.

name: unix_bpf_recvmsg
prose: recvmsg handler for a unix socket with a BPF psock. Returns -EOPNOTSUPP if flags has MSG_OOB; returns 0 if len is 0; if sk_psock_get(sk) returns NULL it returns __unix_recvmsg(sk, msg, len, flags). Otherwise, with a psock reference held, it takes u->iolock (mutex_lock). If sk->sk_receive_queue is non-empty and the psock queue is empty it releases the mutex, drops the psock with sk_psock_put and returns __unix_recvmsg(...). Otherwise it calls sk_msg_recvmsg: a nonzero result (a byte count or a negative errno such as -EFAULT) is returned after releasing the mutex and the psock. If the result is 0 it computes timeo with sock_rcvtimeo and calls unix_msg_wait_data, which returns 1 when sk->sk_shutdown has RCV_SHUTDOWN (without checking for data), 0 when timeo is 0, and otherwise may release and retake u->iolock while waiting and returns whether any data (receive queue, psock ingress_skb or ingress_msg) exists. If it returns nonzero: if the psock queue is not empty it retries sk_msg_recvmsg; if it is empty it releases the mutex and psock and returns __unix_recvmsg(...) (this includes the RCV_SHUTDOWN case with no data). If it returns 0 the result is -EAGAIN. On the paths after the psock was obtained the mutex is released and sk_psock_put is called before returning.
note: Checked unix_bpf.c:16-96. Reviewer round-15 right: 'data is available' misdescribes the RCV_SHUTDOWN case (unix_msg_wait_data returns 1 at line 23-24 without data); round-1 (negative errno from sk_msg_recvmsg returned directly) and round-2 (native recvmsg on shutdown with empty psock queue) are right about the older prose and are now explicit.

name: vsock_connectible_wait_data
prose: Waits until a connected vsock socket has data to receive, an error or shutdown is seen, or the timeout expires. Preconditions: the caller holds the socket lock; wait is an initialised wait entry; recv_data may be NULL, and if not NULL vsk->transport is non-NULL and provides notify_recv_pre_block. Loop: prepare_to_wait; data = vsock_connectible_has_data(vsk); if data != 0 (positive or negative) leave the loop; if sk->sk_err is nonzero, or sk->sk_shutdown has RCV_SHUTDOWN, or vsk->peer_shutdown has SEND_SHUTDOWN, leave the loop with err 0; if timeout is 0, err = -EAGAIN and leave; if recv_data is non-NULL call transport->notify_recv_pre_block and leave with its error if negative; otherwise release_sock, schedule_timeout, lock_sock, then if a signal is pending err = sock_intr_errno(timeout) and leave, else if the remaining timeout is 0 err = -EAGAIN and leave. Every loop exit goes through finish_wait, and the socket lock is held again when the function returns. After the loop it returns err if nonzero, otherwise -ENOMEM if data is negative, otherwise data (0 when the loop ended because of an error or shutdown with no data, or a positive value from vsock_connectible_has_data converted to int).
note: Checked af_vsock.c:2239-2304. Prose kept in substance: the original reviewer's claim that timeout returns -EAGAIN, not 0, is already what the code and the old prose say (2267-2270, 2285-2287). Replaced 'always removes wait' by the single loop-exit statement.

name: __vsock_stream_recvmsg
prose: Static function that receives from a connected SOCK_STREAM vsock socket; the caller holds the socket lock and vsk->transport is non-NULL. target = sock_rcvlowat(sk, flags & MSG_WAITALL, len). Returns -ENOMEM at once if target >= transport->stream_rcvhiwat(vsk); returns the negative error of transport->notify_recv_init if it fails. Then it loops: vsock_connectible_wait_data with a result <= 0 leaves the loop (err = that result: 0, -EAGAIN, sock_intr_errno(timeout), -ENOMEM or a negative notify_recv_pre_block error); notify_recv_pre_dequeue with a negative result leaves the loop; transport->stream_dequeue(vsk, msg, len - copied, flags) with a negative result leaves the loop with that error; the dequeued bytes are added to copied; transport->notify_recv_post_dequeue (called with !(flags & MSG_PEEK) as the 'consume' argument) with a negative result returns that error immediately, even if copied is positive; the loop also ends when read >= target or MSG_PEEK is set, otherwise target is reduced by read and it continues. After the loop (all exits except the immediate returns above): if sk->sk_err is nonzero err = -sk->sk_err, else if sk->sk_shutdown has RCV_SHUTDOWN err = 0; then if copied > 0 the return value is copied, overriding any of these. So the function can return a positive count smaller than target (e.g. after a timeout, signal, error or shutdown following a partial read), and with copied == 0 it returns the loop error, -sk_err, or 0 on local receive shutdown.
note: Checked af_vsock.c:2306-2383. Reviewer claim (partial copied < target on timeout/signal) matches the code (2373-2379: copied > 0 overrides err) and the old prose already stated that copied > 0 overrides wait errors; prose kept in substance with the loop structure made explicit. Removed the claim about what MSG_PEEK does to the receive queue (that is up to the transport's stream_dequeue).

name: __vsock_seqpacket_recvmsg
prose: Static function that receives one message from a connected SOCK_SEQPACKET vsock socket; the caller holds the socket lock and vsk->transport is non-NULL. It calls vsock_connectible_wait_data(sk, &wait, timeout, NULL, 0); if the result is <= 0 it returns it (0 when an error, local receive shutdown or peer send shutdown was seen with no data, -EAGAIN on timeout, sock_intr_errno(timeout) on a signal, -ENOMEM on an internal data-check error). Otherwise it calls transport->seqpacket_dequeue(vsk, msg, flags) and returns its negative result if it fails. After a successful dequeue: if sk->sk_err is nonzero it returns -sk->sk_err; else if sk->sk_shutdown has RCV_SHUTDOWN it returns 0; else it returns msg_len (the dequeued message length) when MSG_TRUNC is set in flags, and len - msg_data_left(msg) (bytes copied into the user buffer) otherwise; in this last branch, if msg_len > len it also sets MSG_TRUNC in msg->msg_flags.
note: Checked af_vsock.c:2385-2433. Reviewer claim (bytes copied, not message length, unless MSG_TRUNC) is already what the old prose said (2419-2422); prose kept, wording tightened.

name: __vsock_connectible_recvmsg
prose: Non-static recvmsg implementation for connection-oriented vsock sockets (stream and seqpacket). The caller does not hold the socket lock. If flags has MSG_ERRQUEUE it returns sock_recv_errqueue(sk, msg, len, SOL_VSOCK, VSOCK_RECVERR) before taking the lock. Otherwise it calls lock_sock(sk), and every later return goes through the out label which calls release_sock. With the lock held: if there is no transport or sk->sk_state is not TCP_ESTABLISHED it returns 0 if SOCK_DONE is set and -ENOTCONN otherwise; if flags has MSG_OOB it returns -EOPNOTSUPP; if sk->sk_shutdown has RCV_SHUTDOWN it returns 0; if len is 0 it returns 0. Otherwise it returns __vsock_stream_recvmsg(sk, msg, len, flags) for SOCK_STREAM sockets and __vsock_seqpacket_recvmsg(sk, msg, len, flags) for all other types; those results can be a positive byte count, 0, or a negative errno (see those functions), and may leave data copied into msg and msg->msg_flags changed.
note: Checked af_vsock.c:2436-2500. Reviewer claims (MSG_ERRQUEUE returns before lock_sock; other errnos possible) are right and already in the old prose. Changed 'otherwise seqpacket' to 'all other socket types' because the code takes the else branch for any type other than SOCK_STREAM. Removed the list of specific errnos (they come from the callees).

name: hvs_do_close_lock_held
prose: Static void function for the Hyper-V vsock transport; the caller holds the socket lock. It sets SOCK_DONE on the socket, writes SHUTDOWN_MASK to vsk->peer_shutdown (WRITE_ONCE), sets sk->sk_state to TCP_CLOSING if vsock_stream_has_data(vsk) <= 0 (otherwise the state is not changed), and calls sk->sk_state_change(sk). Then, only if vsk->close_work_scheduled is true and either cancel_timeout is false or cancel_delayed_work(&vsk->close_work) returns nonzero, it clears close_work_scheduled, calls vsock_remove_sock(vsk) and drops one socket reference with sock_put(sk) (the one taken when the close timeout was scheduled). In all other cases (no scheduled close work, or cancel_timeout true and the cancel fails) it does none of those three steps; when cancel_timeout is false and close work is scheduled the work is not cancelled but the three steps are still done.
note: Checked hyperv_transport.c:261-279. Both reviewer claims were wrong about the current prose: it already made the removal and sock_put conditional on close_work_scheduled and on (!cancel_timeout || cancel succeeds). Prose kept; last sentence added to be explicit about the cancel_timeout=false case.

name: vmci_transport_recv_listen
prose: Static function that handles a packet pkt received on a listening VMCI vsock socket sk. First it looks for a pending child with vmci_transport_get_pending(sk, pkt). If one is found it is locked (lock_sock), its local CID is set to pkt->dg.dst.context, and if its sk_state is TCP_SYN_SENT the result is vmci_transport_recv_connecting_server(sk, pending, pkt), otherwise a reset is sent with vmci_transport_send_reset(pending, pkt) and the result is -EINVAL; if the result is negative the child is removed with vsock_remove_pending and sk_acceptq_removed; the child is then unlocked and released with vmci_transport_release_pending, and the result is returned. If no pending child is found: a packet that is not REQUEST or REQUEST2 gets vmci_transport_reply_reset and -EINVAL; pkt->u.size == 0 gets a reply reset and -EINVAL; a full accept queue gets a reply reset and -ECONNREFUSED; failure of vsock_create_connected sends a reset and returns -ENOMEM. Otherwise the child gets local and remote addresses from the packet, vsock_assign_transport is called; if it fails or vmci_check_transport(child) is false it sends a reset, calls sock_put on the child and returns err (which is 0 if only the check failed). It then picks qp_size (the packet's size if within the child's buffer_min/max sizes, else the child's buffer_size), decides between REQUEST and REQUEST2 handling, and sends a negotiate (or negotiate2) packet, or sets -EINVAL if no notify structure or no common protocol version exists. If that result is negative it sends a reset, calls sock_put on the child, converts the error with vmci_transport_error_to_vsock_error and returns it. On success it adds the child to the pending list (vsock_add_pending, sk_acceptq_added), sets its state TCP_SYN_SENT, sets its produce/consume/buffer sizes to qp_size, calls notify_ops->process_request, sets vpending->listener to sk, takes references with sock_hold on both sk and the child, schedules vpending->pending_work after HZ and returns the nonnegative result of the negotiate send.
note: slice cut the head (function at vmci_transport.c:968-1157). Reviewer round-15 claim (pending-socket logic belongs to recv_pkt) is wrong: the pending lookup/handling is at lines 985-1012 of this function. Checked 968-1157.

name: nl80211_channel_switch
prose: Handles the nl80211 channel switch command for a device. Returns -EOPNOTSUPP if the driver has no channel_switch op or the wiphy lacks WIPHY_FLAG_HAS_CHANNEL_SWITCH. By interface type: AP and P2P-GO need a new beacon and do not require the handle-DFS flag, and return -ENOTCONN if the link's ap.beacon_interval is 0; IBSS returns -ENOTCONN if ssid_len is 0; mesh point returns -ENOTCONN if id_len is 0; any other type returns -EOPNOTSUPP. These returns happen before any allocation. After zeroing params it returns -EINVAL if NL80211_ATTR_WIPHY_FREQ or CH_SWITCH_COUNT is missing, if a new beacon is needed and CSA_IES is missing, or if the count exceeds 255. For AP/P2P-GO it parses the beacon-after (nl80211_parse_beacon), allocates the csa_attrs array (-ENOMEM on failure), parses the nested CSA attributes and the CSA beacon, requires NL80211_ATTR_CNTDWN_OFFS_BEACON (-EINVAL if absent) and parses counter offsets for the beacon and probe response, any of these errors being returned. For all types it then parses the chandef, returns -EINVAL if cfg80211_reg_can_beacon_relax fails, returns the negative result of cfg80211_chandef_dfs_required, and if DFS is required sets radar_required and returns -EINVAL when the handle-DFS flag is absent but only for IBSS and mesh point (need_handle_dfs_flag is true only for those). It sets block_tx if requested, for AP/P2P-GO with an unsolicited broadcast probe response attribute it parses it (error returned), sets link_id and returns rdev_channel_switch(...) as is. Every return after the allocation point passes through the free label, which kfree()s beacon_after and beacon_csa mbssid_ies and rnr_ies and csa_attrs; the earlier returns allocate nothing.
note: slice cut the head (function at nl80211.c:11488-11651). Reviewer round-15 claim is wrong about which types need the flag: for AP/P2P-GO need_handle_dfs_flag is set false (11514) and it stays true (default) for IBSS/mesh (11498), so -EINVAL on a missing HANDLE_DFS happens for IBSS/mesh, not AP/GO; but the old prose's 'DFS channel without the handle-DFS flag' was too general, and its 'in every case frees' was imprecise, both fixed.

name: nl80211_set_pmk
prose: Handles the nl80211 set-PMK command. Returns -EOPNOTSUPP if the interface type is neither station nor P2P client, or if the wiphy lacks NL80211_EXT_FEATURE_4WAY_HANDSHAKE_STA_1X. Returns -EINVAL if NL80211_ATTR_MAC or NL80211_ATTR_PMK is missing. Returns -ENOTCONN if wdev->connected is false (not -EINVAL). Returns -EINVAL if the MAC attribute differs from wdev->u.client.connected_addr, or if the PMK length is neither WLAN_PMK_LEN nor WLAN_PMK_LEN_SUITE_B_192. Otherwise it builds a cfg80211_pmk_conf (aa, pmk, pmk_len and, if NL80211_ATTR_PMKR0_NAME is present, pmk_r0_name) and returns rdev_set_pmk(rdev, dev, &pmk_conf), whose result may be zero or a negative error from the driver. rdev_set_pmk is not called on any of the earlier returns.
note: Checked nl80211.c:17300-17336. Reviewer round-15 right: not connected returns -ENOTCONN only (17318-17319); round-1 (driver error may be returned) right and now explicit.

name: nl80211_send_wiphy
prose: Fills a netlink message with wiphy attributes for one dump step. Parameters: rdev, cmd, msg, portid, seq, flags, state (struct nl80211_dump_wiphy_state, must be non-NULL). Returns -ENOBUFS if nl80211hdr_put fails; returns -EINVAL if state is NULL (after the header was put, without cancelling the message); returns -EMSGSIZE after genlmsg_cancel(msg, hdr) if any attribute does not fit. Otherwise it adds the wiphy index, name and generation attributes; if cmd is not NL80211_CMD_NEW_WIPHY it stops there (state is not changed), calls genlmsg_end and returns 0. For NL80211_CMD_NEW_WIPHY it switches on state->split_start (values 0 to 18 each add a group of attributes; other values add nothing) and advances state: in split mode (state->split) each stage increments split_start and stops, except that the iftype-extended-capability part of stage 13 can break out without incrementing split_start, after setting state->capa_start, when more capabilities remain; in unsplit mode the stages from 0 through 8 are emitted and split_start is reset to 0; the last stage (18) also sets split_start to 0. After the switch it calls genlmsg_end(msg, hdr) and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head (function at nl80211.c:2732-3394). Reviewer claim (success returns genlmsg_end length, not 0) is wrong: lines 3387-3389 call genlmsg_end then 'return 0'. Prose kept in substance; added exact conditions for each return and the split stepping.

name: nl80211_new_station
prose: Handles the nl80211 new-station command (the packet called it nl80211_add_station). Returns -EOPNOTSUPP if the driver has no add_station op; -EINVAL if NL80211_ATTR_MAC, STA_LISTEN_INTERVAL or STA_SUPPORTED_RATES is missing, or if neither STA_AID nor PEER_AID is present; if MLD_ADDR is given the MAC attribute becomes the link MAC and -EINVAL is returned if it is not a valid Ethernet address. It copies optional attributes (VLAN id, P2P PS, AID, capability, extended capability, HT, VHT, HE, EHT, UHR, EML, 6 GHz HE, S1G, opmode notification, plink action, airtime weight) into a station_parameters block, returning -EINVAL if an EHT capability fails ieee80211_eht_capa_size_ok against the HE capability or if a UHR capability is given without an EHT capability, and -EOPNOTSUPP if a nonzero airtime weight is given on a wiphy without NL80211_EXT_FEATURE_AIRTIME_FAIRNESS. It returns the errors of nl80211_parse_sta_txpower_setting, nl80211_parse_sta_channel_info and nl80211_parse_sta_wme, -EINVAL if parse_station_flags fails, and, when the WME flag is not set, clears HT and VHT and returns -EINVAL if HE, 6 GHz HE, EHT or UHR capabilities are present; it returns -EINVAL if a 6 GHz HE capability is combined with HT or VHT. Then by interface type. AP, AP_VLAN and P2P_GO: clears the uAPSD modify bit if the wiphy lacks WIPHY_FLAG_AP_UAPSD or the station lacks the WME flag; -EINVAL for a TDLS peer flag or a PEER_AID attribute; removes the TDLS peer bit from the flag mask; -EINVAL if the authenticated/associated flags are in the mask without NL80211_FEATURE_FULL_AP_CLIENT_STATE, or the SPP A-MSDU flag is in the mask without NL80211_EXT_FEATURE_SPP_AMSDU_SUPPORT; if neither auth nor assoc is in the mask it adds both to mask and set; params.vlan = get_vlan(info, rdev), and an error pointer is returned with PTR_ERR. Mesh point: clears the uAPSD bit; -EINVAL if the associated flag is in the mask or for a TDLS peer flag or PEER_AID. Station and P2P client: clears the uAPSD bit; -EINVAL if authenticated/associated flags are in the mask or the TDLS peer flag is not set; -EOPNOTSUPP if the wiphy lacks WIPHY_FLAG_SUPPORTS_TDLS or WIPHY_FLAG_TDLS_EXTERNAL_SETUP; removes the authorized bit from the flag mask. Any other type returns -EOPNOTSUPP. After the switch, with the link id from the request: if wdev->valid_links is set, a negative link id gives -EINVAL and one not in valid_links gives -ENOLINK; if it is not set, a non-negative link id gives -EINVAL; these go to the out label. Finally it sets params.epp_peer from the EPP_PEER attribute and returns rdev_add_station(rdev, dev, mac_addr, &params). The out label calls dev_put(params.vlan) (NULL for types other than AP, AP_VLAN and P2P_GO, or without a VLAN attribute, in which case dev_put on NULL does nothing); returns before get_vlan and the get_vlan error return do not reach it.
note: Real function is nl80211_new_station (nl80211.c:8637-8946); there is no nl80211_add_station in the file (grep finds only nl80211_new_station), so the name was wrong and the slice cut the head. Old prose said an airtime weight without support gives -EINVAL (code: -EOPNOTSUPP at 8786-8789) and misnamed the parameter block; rewritten from the full function.

name: __reg_process_hint_country_ie
prose: Static function returning an enum reg_request_treatment (and, in one case, the negative errno -EINVAL cast to that type). It reads the last regulatory request with get_last_request() (rcu_dereference_rtnl, so the caller must hold the RCU read lock or RTNL). It modifies nothing. If the last request is cell-base: returns REG_REQ_IGNORE if regdom_changes(country_ie_request->alpha2) and REG_REQ_ALREADY_SET if not. Otherwise, if wiphy->regulatory_flags has REGULATORY_COUNTRY_IE_IGNORE it returns REG_REQ_IGNORE. Then it returns -EINVAL if country_ie_request->alpha2 is not a valid alpha2 (is_an_alpha2). If the last request's initiator is not NL80211_REGDOM_SET_BY_COUNTRY_IE it returns REG_REQ_OK. Otherwise it looks up the last request's wiphy: if it is a different wiphy than wiphy it returns REG_REQ_IGNORE when the alpha2 changes the current regdomain and REG_REQ_ALREADY_SET when it does not; if it is the same wiphy it returns REG_REQ_OK when regdom_changes is true and REG_REQ_ALREADY_SET when it is false.
note: slice cut the head (function at reg.c:2832-2871). Both reviewer round-15 claims are wrong: an invalid alpha2 returns -EINVAL (2848-2849), and the same-wiphy unchanged alpha2 returns REG_REQ_ALREADY_SET (2868-2870). Old prose was correct in outcome; rewritten in code order for clarity.

name: cfg80211_connect
prose: Starts a connection attempt for the station interface dev; the caller holds the wiphy lock (lockdep_assert_wiphy). Returns -EALREADY, changing nothing, if wdev->u.client.ssid_len is nonzero and either differs from connect->ssid_len or the stored SSID differs from connect->ssid; or if wdev->connected and prev_bssid is NULL. Returns -ENOTCONN, changing nothing, if wdev->connected and prev_bssid differs from wdev->u.client.connected_addr. Returns -EINPROGRESS, changing nothing, if wdev->connect_keys is non-NULL. After those checks it ANDs connect->ht_capa_mask and vht_capa_mask with the wiphy's ht/vht capa_mod_mask (a modification of connect that remains even on later errors). If connkeys is non-NULL and connkeys->def >= 0, and the default key's cipher is WEP40 or WEP104, it sets connect->key_idx, key and key_len from that key and, where unset, connect->crypto.cipher_group and the single pairwise cipher to that cipher; for other ciphers the key fields of connect are left as they were. If connkeys is non-NULL with def < 0 it WARNs and returns -EINVAL; if connkeys is NULL it sets connect->key to NULL and key_len and key_idx to 0. It then sets wdev->connect_keys = connkeys, copies connect->ssid into wdev->u.client.ssid and sets ssid_len, sets wdev->conn_bss_type from connect->pbss, and calls cfg80211_sme_connect(wdev, connect, prev_bssid) if rdev->ops->connect is NULL and rdev_connect(rdev, dev, connect) otherwise. If that returns an error it sets wdev->connect_keys back to NULL, clears wdev->u.client.ssid_len only when wdev->connected is false, and returns the error; connkeys itself is not freed here. Otherwise it returns 0, leaving the SSID, ssid_len and connect_keys in wdev.
note: Checked sme.c:1436-1543. Reviewer round-15 right: key/key_idx are filled only for WEP40/WEP104 ciphers (1489-1506). Reviewer round-2 (mask ANDing after the -EINPROGRESS check) right and already reflected in old prose ordering; original claims (ssid_len not cleared when connected; may call SME connect) already in old prose. Prior prose 'always fills' for def >= 0 corrected.

name: cfg80211_sme_connect
prose: Software-SME connect step for wdev; the caller holds the wiphy lock. Returns -EOPNOTSUPP, changing nothing, if the driver lacks either the auth or the assoc op. Otherwise it calls cfg80211_wdev_release_bsses(wdev); if wdev->connected is true it calls cfg80211_sme_free(wdev) and sets wdev->connected to false. If wdev->conn is already non-NULL it returns -EINPROGRESS and leaves that conn in place (the earlier release and connected changes remain). Otherwise it allocates wdev->conn with kzalloc (-ENOMEM, conn stays NULL, if that fails), copies *connect into conn->params (pointing params.bssid at conn->bssid and copying the BSSID when connect->bssid is non-NULL), and builds the connection IEs with cfg80211_sme_get_conn_ies; if that fails it kfree()s wdev->conn directly (not via cfg80211_sme_free), sets it to NULL and returns -ENOMEM. Otherwise it sets params.ie, sets auto_auth and starts with open-system auth when connect->auth_type is NL80211_AUTHTYPE_AUTOMATIC (auto_auth false otherwise), sets params.ssid and ssid_len from wdev->u.client, looks up a matching bss with cfg80211_get_bss, and copies prev_bssid into conn->prev_bssid and sets prev_bssid_valid if prev_bssid is non-NULL. If a bss was found it calls cfg80211_step_auth_next and cfg80211_conn_do_work and then cfg80211_put_bss; if not, it calls cfg80211_conn_scan and turns -EBUSY into 0 while setting conn->state to CFG80211_CONN_SCAN_AGAIN. If the resulting err is nonzero it calls cfg80211_sme_free(wdev) (freeing the new conn); it returns err (0, or an error from cfg80211_conn_do_work or cfg80211_conn_scan).
note: slice cut the head (function at sme.c:552-646). Reviewer round-1 (existing conn not freed on -EINPROGRESS) and round-2 (kzalloc failure has no conn; get_conn_ies path frees directly) are right and are stated explicitly now; old prose was already largely accurate about both.

name: cfg80211_is_all_idle
prose: Returns true if no wireless device of any registered wiphy is connected, connecting or beaconing. The caller must hold RTNL (for_each_rdev asserts it with ASSERT_RTNL; disconnect_work calls it under rtnl_lock). It iterates all registered devices; for each it takes the wiphy lock (guard(wiphy)) for the duration of that device's scan and walks every wdev in rdev->wiphy.wdev_list; if any wdev has a non-NULL conn, or wdev->connected set, or cfg80211_beaconing_iface_active(wdev) true, it records that the result is false but still continues through all remaining devices. It returns true if no wdev matched (including when there are none) and false otherwise.
note: slice cut the head (function at sme.c:678-703). Reviewer round-2 right (RTNL is a precondition via for_each_rdev_check_rtnl in core.h:181-185); round-1 about the vacuous contract is irrelevant now since the contract is left empty (global state and locking). Checked 678-703.
